title: Large personal Amiga/ST/DOS engines and language recovery discovery
summary: Personally screen 611 candidate URLs and add 16 projects, with seven explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root personally searched 18 GitHub query routes, screened 611 unique URLs and inspected 23 pinned repository trees. Sixteen additions and seven explicit non-promotions. One additional large archive tree was unavailable and is not counted as reviewed. Native semantic recovery, original-data ports, behavioral application reconstruction and historical source preservation are separated from static CPU recompilation, new tooling and wrong-platform remakes. No upstream code or service was executed.

sources.reason: Enhanced branch of recovered Populous engine, retaining typed terrain rules and original order-record layout alongside new HD mesh rendering. Inspected simulation structures and HD close-up projection code.
Extracts original STX dungeon, texts, rules tables and images into a new cc65 engine. Inspected STX sector/database reader and creature-group handling.

Classic composition engine reconstructs documented and black-box-observed Tunesmith behavior. Inspected rhythm implementation and evidence-tagged specification separating observation, inference and unknowns.

Implements historical column/series traversal, linked heads and skip/rest/loop semantics from Fingers manual. Inspected detailed traversal rules and code rather than relying only on visual resemblance.
Parses QB 4.5 OMF records/relocations and symbolically lifts x87/runtime calls to BASIC statements. Inspected statement separator and expression reconstruction logic.
Rewritten AGI development system decodes, edits and recompiles historical logic, picture, view and sound resources. Inspected raw VOL/DIR resource ownership and serialization model.
Viewer/decompiler for several SCUMM container generations, graphics, scripts and sound. Inspected explicit v5 big-endian block/container parsing and ScummVM-derived resource iterator lineage.
Extracts/packs MEMLIST resources and converts original game-language bytecode to editable assembly and back. Inspected explicit bank/offset/size record reader.
Function-level C reconstruction with typed static data and native host. Inspected automap geometry/clipping routines with original canonical addresses, not generic CPU dispatch.
Normalizes original 502-byte PARTY.SAV and ScummVM slots for editing/export while preserving untouched monster/metadata payloads. Inspected gzip slot and field layout handling.
Refactors Bethke 1998 library over Spencer/NetBSD engine while retaining four-LVO ABI. Inspected original-attributed matching engine and register-call wrapper.

Preserves 1987–1997 DOS applications including TAP time administration, SO_NEW vocabulary and RMS timetables, with original and print-recovered sources distinguished. Inspected TAP calendar code and provenance.
Recreates vintage BASIC language/compiler behavior with DOS MZ/COM/OMF output and modern backends. Inspected historical control-flow parser and documented original-compiler comparison contract.
Native C11 reconstruction from Ghidra output with per-function original 68000 comparisons and typed game systems. Inspected spell/mana/timeline implementation.

Rewrites 1995 annotated Entombed/Smaky source routine-by-routine into Scala state machine, retaining original memory layout. Inspected man movement/collision semantic code separately from 68000 reference interpreter.
Targets released MS-DOS 1.25 ASM.ASM source with parsing, liveness, function-entry and C-emission analysis. Inspected actual hardcoded subject path and analysis pipeline.

Shipped runtime is primarily static 68000 recompilation over a machine struct and program-counter switch; partial native car routines retain machine-state contracts. No-Musashi gate proves library exclusion, not removal of instruction-level execution. Retain for audit, not full native recovery.

Recovers 1996 Windows CD resources and newly implements rules from sprites/help text. Original ST/Amiga title history does not make this a recovered ST/Amiga engine; source-platform mismatch for this focused pass.
Preserved 1993 demo source with possible damaged files, not a game/application in the current requested focus. Relevant broader scene-source lead.
Preserved 1992 Suspect demo source, not the similarly named game. Damaged disks and older non-final source documented; do not conflate identities.
New Device Tree configuration parser for Amiga, not reconstruction of a historical Amiga application. Platform support alone is insufficient for this batch.

Generic DOS EXE decompiler tooling with minimal README, not a named reconstructed game/application. Do not confuse with Exhumed/Powerslave game or assume identity with separately tracked Exhume toolkit.
Java/libGDX remake reproduces published game concept, but original executable/data-format or source-recovery evidence not established in reviewed tree and README.
